eyebrow: The T-SQL Development Course · Chapter Nine
subtitle: Lesson 96 · The Default · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: You've been using this all along
code:
-- No SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL line at all --
-- this already runs under READ COMMITTED.
SELECT ProductID, Name, ListPrice
FROM Production.Product
WHERE ListPrice > 1000;
caption: SQL Server's default for every new connection, no exceptions.

code:
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;
-- Every read sees only COMMITTED data.
-- Lesson 92's dirty read cannot happen here --
-- Session B's read would simply BLOCK instead.
caption: The one guarantee every level from here up always provides.

eyebrow: What it still allows -- and why
code:
-- Shared locks are held only for each
-- STATEMENT's read, not the whole transaction.
-- The lock releases the instant that SELECT finishes --
-- leaving room for nonrepeatable + phantom reads.
caption: Lessons 93 and 94's anomalies both slip through this exact gap.

eyebrow: Checking what level you're actually on
code:
DBCC USEROPTIONS;
-- Look for the "isolation level" row.
caption: Easy to forget you changed this earlier in a session -- always verify.
